changed.title: Find a binary De Morgan formula below the parity-lane leaf bound for full cyclic window tables
changed.statement:
∃ d extra a q : ℕ,
  let k := d + 1
  let w := k + extra
  let m := a + 1
  let n := m * k + q * (k + 1)
  let hn : 0 < n := Nat.add_pos_left (Nat.mul_pos (Nat.succ_pos a) (Nat.succ_pos d)) _
  let stride := 2 ^ (w + 1)
  let I := n * stride
  ∃ F : PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.DMFormula I,
    (∀ table : Fin n → (Fin (w + 1) → Bool) → Bool,
      let inputs := fun addr : Fin I =>
        table ⟨(addr.val / stride) % n, Nat.mod_lt _ hn⟩ (fun bit => addr.val.testBit bit.val)
      F.eval inputs = true ↔ ∃ word : Fin n → Bool, ∀ i : Fin n,
        table i (fun k => word ⟨(i.val + k.val) % n, Nat.mod_lt _ hn⟩) = true) ∧
    F.leaves < 2 ^ d * m ^ 2
changed.unlocks: tests the proposed leaf floor for full cyclic window table decision formulas
changed.context: We hold no formula below the proposed bound. Try k=2, m=10, q=0 and w=2, where the target is fewer than 200 leaves on 160 raw bits. The alternating tag restrictions in the parity argument charge disjoint sets of occurrences. Test whether a signed-literal tree can reuse a factor across tags without changing the answer on tables outside those restrictions. Count each occurrence and verify the universal cyclic-word test on the full table.

changed.title: Twice the matching rank in fixed phase determinant queries identifies all complex matching products even on subboards
changed.statement:
∀ (n : ℕ) (H : Fin n → Fin n → Bool),
  let I := Fin n
  let E := I × I
  let V := Submodule.span ℚ {v : E → ℚ | ∃ π : Equiv.Perm I, (∀ j, H (π j) j = true) ∧
    v = fun e => if π e.2 = e.1 then (1 : ℚ) else 0}
  let d := Module.finrank ℚ V
  let edge := fun (i j : I) => 2^(i.val*n+j.val)
  ∃ (powers : Fin (2*d) → ℕ) (bad : Finset ℂ),
    (∀ z : ℂ, z ∉ bad → ∃ read : (Fin (2*d) → ℂ) → Equiv.Perm I → ℂ,
      ∀ A : Matrix I I ℂ, (∀ i j, H i j = false → A i j = 0) →
        ∀ π : Equiv.Perm I,
        read (fun h => Matrix.det (fun i j => A i j * z^(powers h * edge i j) : Matrix I I ℂ)) π =
          ∏ j : I, A (π j) j) ∧
    ∃ q₀ : ℕ, ∀ q : ℕ, q₀ ≤ q → ∀ ζ : ℂ, IsPrimitiveRoot ζ q → ζ ∉ bad
changed.unlocks: Recovers every complex matching product on any prescribed mask with a fixed list of phase determinant evaluations.
changed.context: Use binary place values for edges. In the determinant expansion a permutation gets the sum of the place values on its matching, distinct for every permutation. Supported monomials have degree n and incidence rank d. Apply the sampling certificate, then substitute t_h=z^(L^h) with L larger than every exponent in the certificate. Distinct terms retain distinct powers, leaving a nonzero univariate polynomial. Exclude its finitely many roots. The remaining evaluations determine all matching products, and the excluded roots have bounded finite orders whenever they are roots of unity.

changed.title: Two questions short of exact recovery on the singular spacing-two column bank
changed.statement:
∀ (t : ℕ) (ht : 0 < t), 2 ≤ t →
  let h := 3*t-4
  letI : ∀ p : Prop, Decidable p := Classical.propDecidable
  let F := ZMod 2
  let n := 6*t
  let W := Fin n → F
  let ix := fun j : ℕ => (⟨j % n, Nat.mod_lt _ (Nat.mul_pos (Nat.zero_lt_succ 5) ht)⟩ : Fin n)
  let rot := fun (s : ℕ) (w : W) (i : Fin n) => w (ix (i.val + n - s % n))
  let out := fun (name c raw : W) (i : Fin n) =>
    let old := rot 3 raw + name
    let y := fun j : Fin n => old j + old (ix (j.val+2)) + old (ix (j.val+n-2))
    y i + (1+y (ix (i.val+1)))*y (ix (i.val+2)) + rot 4 raw i + c i
  let run := fun (ask : Fin h → ℕ → W →ₗ[F] F) (w : W) =>
    (List.finRange h).foldl (fun z i => 2*z + (if ask i z w = 0 then 0 else 1)) (0 : ℕ)
  let mix := fun (w : W) (i : Fin n) =>
    let old := rot 3 w
    old i + old (ix (i.val+2)) + old (ix (i.val+n-2))
  let site := fun j : Fin h => if t = 2 then (2+3*j.val) else j.val
  let num := if t = 2 then 21 else 19
  ∀ (name c : W) (fixed : Bool) (k : ℕ),
    (∃ (ask : Fin h → ℕ → W →ₗ[F] F) (A : ℕ → W →ₗ[F] W) (b : ℕ → W),
      (fixed = true → ∀ j p w, ask j p w = mix w (ix (2*site j))) ∧
      k ≤ Nat.card {w : W // out name c w = A (run ask w) w + b (run ask w)}) ↔ 64*k ≤ num*2^n

changed.title: Which parity tests of uniformly chosen depth-one one-hot tables have a uniform joint answer?
changed.statement:
let nonlinear := fun (g : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Gate) =>
  (g.inputs.length == 2) &&
    xor (xor (g.op.eval [false, false]) (g.op.eval [false, true]))
        (xor (g.op.eval [true, false]) (g.op.eval [true, true]))
let depth := fun (w : ℕ) (Q : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) =>
  (Q.gates.foldl (fun (ds : List ℕ) g =>
    ds ++ [(g.inputs.map (fun h => ds.getD h 0)).foldr max 0 + (nonlinear g).toNat])
    (List.replicate w 0)).getD Q.output 0
∀ (a b m t : ℕ),
  let F := ZMod 2
  let M := Matrix (Fin (a+1)) (Fin (b+1)) F
  let T := Fin (a+1) → Fin (b+1) → Bool
  ∀ B : Fin m → M,
    let test := fun (P : T) (D : M) =>
      ∑ x, ∑ y, D x y * (if P x y then (1 : F) else 0)
    let realizable := fun (P : T) => ∃ Q : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit,
      (∀ g ∈ Q.gates, g.inputs.length ≤ 2) ∧
      PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack (a+1+(b+1)) Q ∧ PEqualNP.Represents.Represents P Q ∧
      depth (a+1+(b+1)) Q ≤ 1 ∧ Q.gates.countP nonlinear ≤ t
    let count := fun (v : Fin m → F) => Nat.card {P : T // realizable P ∧ ∀ i, test P (B i) = v i}
    let even := fun (D : M) => (∀ x, (∑ y, D x y) = 0) ∧ (∀ y, (∑ x, D x y) = 0)
    let r := 2*t
    let charge := fun (D : M) =>
      (Nat.card {P : T // realizable P ∧ test P D = 0} : ℤ) -
      (Nat.card {P : T // realizable P ∧ test P D = 1} : ℤ)
    (((∀ u v, count u = count v) ↔ ∀ S : Finset (Fin m), S.Nonempty →
       (if r < min a b then ¬ even (S.sum B) else S.sum B ≠ 0)) ∧
     (r < min a b → ∀ D : M, even D → ∃ z : ℤ, Odd z ∧
       charge D = 2^(a+b+1+Nat.choose (r+1) 2) * z))
changed.unlocks: Decides which collections of parity observations hide the nonlinear budget under uniform sampling of distinct realizable tables.
changed.context: Uniformity means all nontrivial answer characters vanish. Free offsets cancel characters with an odd marginal. On an even mask sum the rank characters through r. Partial Gaussian binomial summation leaves a d=0 term of valuation choose(r+1,2). Each d>0 term gains d(b-r)+choose(d,2) powers of two and all feasible Gaussian coefficients are odd. Thus the interior sum cannot vanish. Add the offset exponent a+b+1. At saturation every table is allowed and ordinary character orthogonality applies.
